At one day, the 90% interval spans only 1.4 units, implying high confidence that short-term realized volatility is relatively contained. The roughly doubling of the interval width at each step is broadly consistent with a square-root-of-time scaling of volatility, suggesting my uncertainty model was relatively conventional and did not embed fat-tailed tail risks as the dominant driver.
